name: OpenVibe.Bot
tagline: Get your robot online in minutes.
description: OpenVibe.Bot is an open control panel for robots. Add a robot, pair it with one command or a QR code, and drive it from any browser with live video, real controls and a stop button that always works. Buy a ready-made bot or bring your own: a Raspberry Pi robot, an ESP32, a ROS 2 robot, a phone, or a Cozmo. Share control, automate it, hand it to your AI agent, and stream it to OpenVibe.Live or openre.stream when you want to.

pillars.title: Pair devices
pillars.text: Revocable device keys and one-time pairing codes, not stream keys.

pillars.title: Share control
pillars.text: Owner, whitelist, queues, timed turns, moderators and apps.

pillars.title: Safe on the device
pillars.text: Dead-man stop, command limits and local emergency stop.

pillars.title: Stream it
pillars.text: Connect a device to a Live stream, a game or a website.

faq.question: Do I need to open ports on my router?
faq.answer: No. The robot connects out to OpenVibe, and video and controls travel over WebRTC, so it works behind ordinary home and mobile networks.

faq.question: Is it only for streaming?
faq.answer: No. Streaming is optional. Bot is a control panel for your robot first: drive it, check on it, share it and automate it.

faq.question: Which robot comes first?
faq.answer: The Adeept 4WD Smart Car Kit for Raspberry Pi: four motors, a pan-tilt camera, distance and line sensors, lights and a buzzer. OpenVibe's device agent drives it directly, so its own open control port never has to be exposed.

faq.question: Does it work with Cozmo?
faq.answer: Yes, built in. Cozmo makes its own Wi-Fi and runs closed firmware, so the OpenVibe agent runs on a computer next to it (a Raspberry Pi or a laptop) that joins Cozmo's Wi-Fi and stays online through another connection. You get driving, the head and lift, its camera, its face display, its voice, lights and cubes, and it stops at edges on its own. No phone app needed.

faq.question: What hardware works?
faq.answer: A Raspberry Pi or another Linux board, an ESP32, a ROS 2 robot, an Android phone, or an ONVIF or RTSP camera. The curated kits list exactly what to buy.

faq.question: How does it keep the robot safe?
faq.answer: The device stops its motors by itself when commands or the connection stop. There is an emergency stop in the panel, limits on speed, range and time, and every command is logged.

faq.question: What will it cost?
faq.answer: Controlling your own robot will not cost anything. Limits and any paid extras will be published before launch.

vision.stepsLead: No port forwarding, no stream keys, no config files.
steps: Name it and pick what it is: a rover, an arm, a camera, a phone on wheels or your own design.
Paste one command on the robot, flash a ready-made card, or scan a QR code. It gets its own key, which you can revoke any time.
Live video and controls in any browser, phone included, with a stop button that always works.

choices.title: Buy one or bring your own
choices.lead: Start with hardware that is known to work, or use what you already have.

items.title: Get a robot
items.text: Curated kits with parts lists, tested settings and build guides, and ready-made bots that arrive paired to your account. The first one on OpenVibe.Bot is the Adeept 4WD Smart Car for Raspberry Pi.

items.title: Bring your own
items.text: Anything with motors, a camera or sensors. Install the OpenVibe device agent on the robot, or, for robots with their own firmware like Cozmo, on a computer next to it, and your robot shows up in the panel.

vision.featuresLead: A control panel for anything you build, whether or not anyone is watching.
features: Drive pad, keyboard, touch joystick and gamepad; buttons, sliders, servos and camera pan-tilt, laid out from your robot's profile.
Video and commands over WebRTC, so driving feels direct. Works behind ordinary home and mobile networks.
Invite friends as operators, or open a public queue with timed turns, cooldowns and per-role limits.
The robot stops itself when commands stop. An emergency stop, speed and range limits and time windows, all logged.
Schedules, triggers and webhooks, plus an API and SDKs for your own apps.
Let your OpenVibe.Actor agent patrol, check on or perform with your robot, with your approval.
vision.connectTitle: Stream it, record it, connect it
vision.connectLead: Optional, one toggle each. Your robot does not need an audience to be useful.
connect: Put the robot's camera on your channel; viewers can drive it from chat or the panel.
Low-latency ingest and restreaming to other platforms from the same camera.
Keep every run as a video and cut clips from it.
vision.building: OpenVibe.Bot is being built now, starting with our own robots; stream-controlled robots already run on OpenVibe.Live.

launch: the Bot service, its device agent and the first robots paired
